name: NY-22
label: Likely D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Mannion at 93-94%, below a fully safe threshold
Mannion holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage and a large cash-on-hand lead
District leans Democratic by about four points with a first-term incumbent running
No public general-election polling is available for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic edge: a D+4 district, incumbency, a favorable environment, and a dominant fundraising position for Mannion over Buller. Prediction markets, however, price the race at 93-94% Democratic rather than fully safe, so the forecast settles at a solid but not overwhelming Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a tighter race, or significant Republican outside spending entering the district, would be the clearest signal to move this toward a tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term Democratic incumbent John Mannion seeks re-election in a Syracuse-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. Mannion has raised roughly $2.7 million and holds about $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with under $200,000 available, leaving the challenger with a steep financial deficit and no reported outside spending on either side so far.

No public general-election polls and no expert race ratings are available, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Mannion's chances around 93-94%, indicating a clear but not absolute Democratic favorite. The forecast expects Mannion to win by a solid double-digit margin, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
